Keywords: Willingness to cooperate on Curonian frontiers
RagShortTexts: Curonian and Samogitian border pressure involved local leaders and Order forces.
A shared opponent did not settle food and home-defense terms of cooperation.

Variants.Content: Samogitian leaders faced Order expeditions and differing demands from allies. Campaigns depended on fodder, roads and home defense. Some favored pursuit while others wanted booty and animals brought home; a common enemy did not end disputes among houses.

Samogitian leaders faced Order expeditions and differing demands from allies. Campaigns depended on fodder, roads and home defense. Some favored pursuit while others wanted booty and animals brought home; a common enemy did not end disputes among houses. Fighters needed food and animals, moving differently with booty on return. Coordinated movement depended on messages, relationships and accepted risks.

Samogitian leaders faced Order expeditions and differing demands from allies. Campaigns depended on fodder, roads and home defense. Some favored pursuit while others wanted booty and animals brought home; a common enemy did not end disputes among houses. Leaders sought people through purposes, shares and defense arrangements. Heavy kin losses weakened later musters, and failed distributions damaged authority.

Samogitian leaders faced Order expeditions and differing demands from allies. Campaigns depended on fodder, roads and home defense. Some favored pursuit while others wanted booty and animals brought home; a common enemy did not end disputes among houses. A household supplying fighters lost labor for fields, animals and repairs. Booty could help, but delay, wounds and animal losses burdened kin and made shared work important.
